- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially when history shows recent upward momentum.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 60+ → 65+), often overshooting by 5–10% in the immediate next period.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 periods, particularly in upward trends — model reacts slower than actual price action.
- Shows strong mean reversion bias: forecasts often revert to historical mean (e.g., 55–58 range) after prolonged deviations, even when true price continues rising.
- Underestimates late-period (last 5–10 days) price increases, especially when true outcome shows accelerating upward momentum.
- Overestimates volatility in early forecast windows, leading to overly conservative (low) forecasts when actual price rises sharply.
- When history includes multiple consecutive high values, model tends to underestimate the next peak, assuming it will not exceed prior highs.
- Forecasts are more accurate when history includes recent price consolidation or sideways movement, but less reliable during sharp trend reversals.
